title: Linters: revive, staticcheck and golangci-lint in the pipeline

videos.script: Lesson 7 ended where go vet stops. Vet reports only what is almost always a bug, so it passes plenty of code a careful reviewer would send back. This lesson is about the tools that make the other trade. {{file}} It starts with one small file. It compiles, vet says nothing, and it has nine problems in it. A deprecated import. A condition that is always true. An error that is thrown away. {{staticcheck}} First, staticcheck. It has a hundred and forty-nine checks in four families, and it finds five of the nine. One of them is a real bug: a guard against dividing by zero that guards nothing. {{revive}} Then revive, which is about style. Names, comments, where a context goes. It surprises people in one way. Out of the box, it never fails a build, whatever it finds. {{golangci}} Next, golangci-lint. One binary, a hundred and fifteen linters, one configuration file. Its defaults report sixteen things on this module, and ten are about dropped errors. Only one of those ten is a clear bug. {{pipeline}} Last, the pipeline. A pinned version, a check that looks only at the lines a change added, and a workflow file. Because a linter that reports two hundred old warnings on its first day is switched off by its second.
